name: Robert Rivas
title: California State Assemblymember, Speaker of the California State Assembly
district: California State Assembly District 29 (Pajaro and Salinas valleys of the Central Coast, including San Benito County and parts of Monterey and Santa Clara counties; represented District 30, largely the same area under the pre-2022 map, from 2018–2022). (Source: official Speaker biography, a29.asmdc.org/biography; Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas.)
years_of_service: First elected to the California State Assembly in November 2018 and took office December 3, 2018 (District 30). Re-elected to the redistricted District 29 seat in 2020 (as District 30), 2022, and 2024, and advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary to the November 3, 2026 general election, in which he is unopposed by a fellow Democrat and faces a Republican challenger. His current Assembly term runs through December 7, 2026. Rivas took the oath of office as the 71st Speaker of the California State Assembly on June 30, 2023, succeeding Anthony Rendon, and continues to serve in that role. California's 12-year consecutive-term limit for the Legislature (in effect since the 2012 elections) means he is not yet term-limited out of the Assembly. (Source: Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas; official Speaker biography, a29.asmdc.org/biography.)
background: Rivas was born January 2, 1980, in Henderson, Nevada, but was raised in Paicines, California, in San Benito County, where his grandfather worked as a farmworker at Almaden Vineyards and, alongside Dolores Huerta and the United Farm Workers, organized for fair contracts. Rivas and his brother grew up in farmworker housing, raised by their single mother and grandparents, who had emigrated from Mexico in the 1960s. He attended public schools in San Juan Bautista and Hollister, graduating from Hollister High School in 1998, and has spoken publicly about growing up with a severe stutter that he continues to manage. He earned a Bachelor's degree in Government from California State University, Sacramento (2003) and a Master's in Public Administration from San José State University (2011). (Source: official Speaker biography, a29.asmdc.org/biography; Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas.)

Before the Legislature, Rivas worked as a student support staff member at San Benito High School, an adjunct professor at Gavilan College, a senior board clerk for the County of Monterey, and a senior field representative for then-Assemblymember (later State Senator) Anna Caballero. In 2010 he was elected to the San Benito County Board of Supervisors, where he served two terms before running for the Assembly. (Source: Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas; official Speaker biography, a29.asmdc.org/biography.)

Rivas was first elected to the Assembly in November 2018, winning an open seat (District 30) with 68.2% of the vote against Republican Neil Kitchens. He was re-elected in 2020 (69.6%), 2022 after redistricting moved his seat to District 29 (63.8%), and 2024 (66.0%), and advanced from the June 2026 top-two primary with 66.3% of the vote. Before becoming Speaker, he chaired the Assembly Agriculture Committee and the Assembly Fairs, Allocation, and Classification Committee, and served as Vice-Chair of the California Latino Legislative Caucus. Assembly Democrats elected him Speaker-designate in November 2022, and he was sworn in as the 71st Speaker of the Assembly on June 30, 2023, succeeding Anthony Rendon. As Speaker, Rivas has made housing affordability, farmworker protections, and cost-of-living relief his signature priorities, and convened a 2024 extraordinary legislative session on gasoline price volatility. (Source: Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas; official Speaker biography, a29.asmdc.org/biography; official 2024 Legislation page, a29.asmdc.org/2024-legislation.)

Rivas's official biography credits him with championing legislation on affordable housing supply, workplace health and safety, the Golden State Teacher Grant Program (a scholarship program for students who commit to teaching in shortage subject areas), the first-in-the-nation COVID-19 Farmworker Relief Package, and the Oil Transportation Safety Act, which strengthened the state's preparedness for spills of non-floating oil along the coast. (Source: official Speaker biography, a29.asmdc.org/biography.)
committee_memberships: As Speaker (June 2023–present), Rivas sits on the Assembly Rules Committee, which he controls through the Speaker's appointment authority over its membership and staff; as the presiding officer, he does not hold regular subject-matter committee seats the way rank-and-file members do, and Ballotpedia's most recent committee-assignment update (September 2023) lists only the Rules Committee for him. (Source: Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas.)

Prior to becoming Speaker, Rivas chaired the Assembly Agriculture Committee (2019–2022) and the Assembly Fairs, Allocation, and Classification Committee (2021–2022), and served as a member of the Assembly Appropriations, Governmental Organization, Judiciary, and Local Government Committees at various points from 2019–2022. (Source: Ballotpedia, Robert Rivas.)
voting_record_highlights: AB 1783 (2019–2020), the Farmworker Housing Act of 2019: Rivas was the lead author. It creates an opt-in, streamlined local-approval process for building farmworker housing on surplus agricultural land, with quality and environmental safeguards. It passed the Senate concurrence vote 57–16 on September 11, 2019, and was signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on October 13, 2019, as Chapter 866, Statutes of 2019. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 1783.)

AB 876 (2023–2024), Pajaro River levee upgrades: Rivas was the lead author, introduced after catastrophic March 2023 flooding in the town of Pajaro. It expedites federal and state work to bring the Pajaro River levee system up to 100-year flood-protection standards. It passed the Senate concurrence vote (Assembly floor) 80–0 and cleared its final Senate committee 11–0, and was signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on October 13, 2023, as Chapter 816, Statutes of 2023. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 876.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation scorecard for Assemblymember/Speaker Rivas was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance record; the public record consists of bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. CalMatters' Digital Democracy project tracks legislators' bill-passage counts and interest-group vote-alignment scores but likewise does not publish a floor-attendance metric, and its Rivas profile page could not be retrieved during this research session (returned a 404).
